claims.text: While Galweg is not directly glossed, in Gnomish gal means "shine (golden, as the Sun)" and "weg" is a masculine suffix.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, "I-Lam na-Ngoldathon: The Grammar and Lexicon of the Gnomish Tongue", in Parma Eldalamberon XI (edited by Christopher Gilson, Arden R. Smith, and Patrick H. Wynne), p. 37

claims.text: Galweg was the father of Failivrin, who fell in love with Túrin when he and his friend Flinding lived in the caverns of the Rodothlim, ruled by Orodreth. He was fond of Túrin, and they often aided one another.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "II. Turambar and the Foalókë": "Notes and Commentary", p. 123; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "II. Turambar and the Foalókë", pp. 82-3

claims.text: Galweg was killed during Melko's attack on the Rodothlim. His dwelling was later occupied by Mîm the Dwarf, who was in turn further slain by Úrin, Túrin's father.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "II. Turambar and the Foalókë", p. 84; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "II. Turambar and the Foalókë", pp. 113-4

claims.text:
In The Lay of the Children of Húrin, written not long after The Book of Lost Tales, Failivrin's father became Orodreth, and the character of Galweg had disappeared entirely.
